# Rainforest to the Coast

> Rainforest to the Coast is the self-guided road trip through Grays Harbor County, Washington, the gateway to the Washington Coast. It links the Quinault Rain Forest and Lake Quinault with the Pacific beaches of Ocean Shores, Seabrook, Pacific Beach, Westport and Grayland, and the harbor towns of Aberdeen and Hoquiam, on one loop off I-5 via US-12 and US-101. Grays Harbor is about 2 hours from Seattle and about 2.5 hours from Portland; the rainforest and the beaches are less than an hour apart. Presented by Grays Harbor Tourism with Ocean Shores Tourism and Experience Westport.

## Plan a trip
- [Trip planner and itineraries (2, 3, 4 and 5 days)](https://www.rainforesttothecoast.com/#planner): builds a day-by-day plan from start city, days, season and interests, with a Google Maps route.
- [The route: five regions](https://www.rainforesttothecoast.com/#route): 1 Quinault (rainforest), 2 Northern Beaches (Ocean Shores, Seabrook, Pacific Beach, Moclips), 3 Southern Beaches (Westport, Grayland, the Cranberry Coast), 4 Port Cities (Aberdeen, Kurt Cobain's hometown, with the Kurt Cobain Museum and Kurt Cobain Memorial Park; Hoquiam), 5 East County (Montesano, Elma, Lake Wynoochee).
- [Where to stay](https://www.rainforesttothecoast.com/#basecamp): Lake Quinault for hikers, Ocean Shores and Seabrook for families and beach walkers, Westport and Grayland for anglers, surfers and seafood.
- [When to go](https://www.rainforesttothecoast.com/#seasons): spring shorebird migration, summer beaches and cranberry blossoms, fall cranberry harvest, winter storm-watching and king tides.
- [Events](https://www.rainforesttothecoast.com/#events): live calendar from Grays Harbor and Ocean Shores.
- [FAQ](https://www.rainforesttothecoast.com/#faq)

## Key facts
- The Quinault Rain Forest is one of the few temperate rain forests in the Western Hemisphere; its Valley of the Giants holds some of the largest trees on Earth.
- Razor clam digs are set by the Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife; check their site for open dates.
- Best time: year-round. Gateway: US-12 from I-5.

## Popular questions (answered on the site's FAQ)
- Kite flying: the wide, windy beaches of Ocean Shores, plus Westport Light State Park, Grayland, Pacific Beach and Moclips.
- Razor clam season and the digging schedule: set by WDFW for Twin Harbors, Copalis and Mocrocks beaches; check wdfw.wa.gov for current dates. Shellfish license required.
- Lake Wynoochee, Wynoochee Falls, Wynoochee Dam and Coho Campground: Olympic National Forest, about 35 miles north of Montesano.
- Kurt Cobain in Aberdeen: Kurt Cobain Memorial Park and the Kurt Cobain Museum (nonprofit Music Project).
- Lady Washington tall ship: home port at the nonprofit Grays Harbor Historical Seaport in Aberdeen.
- Copalis ghost forest: cedars killed by the 1700 Cascadia earthquake, along the Copalis River near Copalis Beach.
- Japanese glass floats and beachcombing: best after winter storms, Moclips to Grayland.
- Dog-friendly beaches: Ocean Shores and most Grays Harbor beaches welcome leashed dogs.
- Towns: Moclips, Humptulips (Humptulips River fishing), Montesano (county seat, Lake Sylvia State Park).
